gaps.sentence: We ___ to Greece for our honeymoon, but that was twenty years ago.
gaps.hint: twenty years ago fixes a finished past
gaps.explanation: A finished time expression like 'twenty years ago' demands the past simple: went.

gaps.sentence: When we were students, we ___ to live on instant noodles.
gaps.hint: a past habit with used to
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' plus the infinitive describes a past habit: used to live.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ to traffic every year for repainting in May.
gaps.explanation: A recurring scheduled event takes the present simple.

gaps.sentence: She ___ two majors when she was at university.
gaps.hint: a completed period in the past
gaps.explanation: A completed past period takes the past simple: did.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ a lot since the new road opened.
gaps.hint: since clause with a present result
gaps.explanation: Change that started in the past and continues to now takes the present perfect: has changed.

gaps.sentence: He rarely ___ his laptop on Sundays because he prefers to rest.
gaps.explanation: Frequency adverbs such as 'rarely' mark habitual actions, which take the present simple: uses.

gaps.sentence: I ___ here for two years, so I know the system well.
gaps.hint: for two years continuing until now
gaps.explanation: 'For two years' with present relevance takes the present perfect, often continuous: have been working.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the car tonight, so take a taxi into town.
gaps.hint: a future activity in progress as reason
gaps.explanation: The future continuous can express something in progress around a future time, here as a polite reason: will be using.
